reskit-test-data/dist2coast.ethos:derivation:
Cut from NASA OBPG's 0.01 degree distance-to-coast grid, which is computed with the Generic Mapping Tools against the GSHHG intermediate-resolution coastline -- exactly what the file's own TIFF tag says.
Verified against the upstream subset: all 576 pixels identical. The only changes are the spatial subset and the netCDF to GeoTIFF container change. No resampling, no rescaling, no change of values at all.

ethos:upstream.note:
Live, but not where this descriptor used to point. The NASA OBPG page it cited for both source and licence -- oceancolor.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/distfromcoast/ -- now 301s to earthdata.nasa.gov/centers/ob-daac, a centre landing page that carries neither the product nor any terms. So the citation that was recorded here no longer substantiates either claim, which is why all three sources above were repointed.
The grid itself is still served, by PacIOOS, who mirrored it from NASA in 2012 and whose ERDDAP endpoint subsets and reprojects on request. That is now the route of record for both the bytes and the terms.

reskit-test-data/esa-cci-landcover.ethos:derivation:
Both files are grid-aligned subsets of ESACCI-LC-L4-LCCS-Map-300m-P1Y-2015-v2.0.7.tif -- the LCCS class layer on the product's native global 300 m grid (129600 x 64800, origin -180/90, 1/360 deg) -- downloaded from CEDA on 2026-09-16 and verified byte-for-byte against the copy catalogued as `esa-cci-landcover`, sha256 5f0030bb0645acae41f7bbc4787e815d57e8034e6d102a458edbf77f568e98e8. No resampling, no reprojection, no class remapping: each clip is an integer pixel window read straight out of that grid, so its cells are the product's own cells.
ESA_CCI_2015_clip.tif is srcWin 66780 13860 540 540, i.e. 5.5-7.0 E by 50.0-51.5 N. 18 LCCS classes.
ESA_CCI_2015_clip_cityBulawayoInZimbabwa.tif is srcWin 74994 39586 170 131 over Bulawayo. 16 LCCS classes.
Both windows are the extents the superseded 2018 clips had, reused exactly so the only variable is the source year: the pixel offsets came out integral to within 0 and 7e-12 of a cell, which also confirms the old clips were cut from this same global grid. Against the 2018 clips 0.84% of cells differ over Aachen and 1.19% over Bulawayo, and the set of classes present is identical in both.
Its extent still follows the old GADM outline; if it is re-cut again, cut it to the OCHA boundary now shipped in the `boundaries` member.

reskit-test-data/icon-lam.ethos:derivation:
ICON-NWP v2.6.4 in limited-area mode (ICON-LAM), 3.3 km native grid over the SASSCAL southern Africa domain, driven by DWD's 13 km global ICON analysis, run on JSC JUWELS under project cjibg36. Per-variable processing and the conservative remap (cdo remapcon) to a regular 0.033 deg lon/lat grid are the same as for icon-lam-southern-africa -- see its ethos:derivation -- including the 10 m wind speed from the components, sqrt(u_10m^2 + v_10m^2), and the power-law 100 m wind speed. Taken from the untiled 2017-2019 files, not from the tiles.
Then, as recorded in the CF history: cdo -L selyear,2019 -selmonth,3 (2023-07-28); cdo seltimestep,1/144 (2025-03-10); and a clip to 14 x 11 cells over Bulawayo, cell centres 28.328-28.757 E by 19.983-20.313 S. The clip is not in the history -- no CDO step for it -- so the window is given here from the coordinates.
Variables are renamed to RESKit's ERA5 convention -- blh, d2m, fdir, fsr, sp, ssrd, t2m, ws10, ws100 -- which is why these files look like ERA5 at a glance. They are not.
The time axis is "days since 2017-01-01" and starts at 789.0, which is 2019-03-01 00:00, so it agrees with the 2019-03 in the filenames. An earlier version of this note called that an oddity; it is not one.

reskit-test-data/srtm.ethos:derivation:
SRTM 1 arc-second resampled to 1/96 degree (37.5 arcsec). Identified from its registration rather than its resolution: the corner sits exactly 0.5 arcsec off the whole degree, which is what a node-registered 1 arcsec grid gives, and the nodata value -32768 is SRTM's void marker. Verified against SRTMGL1 pulled from ESA's STEP server: mean bias -0.003 m, RMSE 2.70 m, 94.6% of cells within 5 m.
The -193 m minimum is the floor of the Hambach open-pit lignite mine, not an error.
